stemMd: What is the purpose of the final sentence of the passage, in which Nando "nodded as though he had read it"?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To reveal that Nando is indifferent to what becomes of the clock.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To show that Nando disapproves of Elena using a laptop on the stairs.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To suggest that Elena has deceived Nando by hiding her real plans.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To show that Nando's eyesight is failing.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To suggest that Nando has guessed what Elena would decide and approves of it.

explanationMd:
A **purpose** question about the last sentence of a story: ask what the ending makes the reader understand.

**What to notice first.** The sentence tells us two things that seem to conflict: Nando "could not possibly have seen the screen", and yet he "nodded as though he had read it". The author has explained why he cannot see (his back is turned), so the nod is not about eyesight.

**The step that settles it.** A nod without having seen the note suggests he knew what she would write before she wrote it. He explained the four-minute offset and then said "Nobody wrote it down"; her note writes it down. His nod suggests he expected it and approves. The unspoken understanding between the two is the point of the ending, and it fits Nando's remark that this was "something one told the next keeper".

**Testing the others.** Failing eyesight, disapproval of the laptop, indifference and deception each need a fact that the passage does not give and that the details contradict.

**How to check.** In a story's last line, look for what the earlier details have been preparing: the unwritten knowledge, Elena's rehearsed speech and Nando's silence all lead to this moment.

distractorRationale.d: The passage gives a different reason he cannot see the screen: he is "standing a few steps below her with his back turned". His eyesight is never mentioned.
distractorRationale.b: Nodding is a sign of agreement, and Nando has shown no objection to the laptop. He does not turn round or comment on it.
distractorRationale.a: His weekly ritual, his care in showing Elena the mechanism and his silent nod all show that he cares. "As though he had read it" shows engagement, not indifference.
distractorRationale.c: Elena does not deceive him: she was silent about the laptop, but her note carries out what he told her. The sentence shows that they understand each other.

accessibilityText: A question about the accompanying short narrative about a tower clock. It asks what the purpose is of the final sentence, in which Nando, standing with his back turned, nods as though he had read the line Elena has typed. Five possible purposes are offered.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Nando could not see the screen but nodded as though he had read it. This implies he had guessed that Elena would keep the four-minute lead, and that he approves. Earlier his flat 'I am sure it will' might hint at indifference (A), but the closing nod undercuts that. Elena deceives no one (C), there is no disapproval of the laptop (B), and eyesight is irrelevant (D). [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: Nando could not have seen the screen, yet he nodded 'as though he had read it'. This implies he foresaw Elena's decision to keep the four-minute lead and agrees with it. A (indifference) is contradicted by the nod of approval, even though his 'weather' tone looks detached earlier. C is wrong because Elena keeps the lead rather than deceiving him, and B and D have no support.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the passage explains that Nando cannot have seen the screen (back turned) and that he had said nothing was written down, so the nod shows he anticipated and approves of what Elena typed; failing eyesight, disapproval, indifference and deception are each contradicted by details in the passage.
